summary: Players run shipping companies hauling goods like tea, spices, and silk between India and Europe, using worker placement to secure ships, cargo, and market actions while a fluctuating supply-and-demand market swings commodity prices. A big part of the game is buying stock in your own and rival companies, so your fortunes are tied not just to trade routes but to how the market values everyone's business.
praised: Dynamic, reactive market that genuinely shifts strategy each game
Meaningful ship-management choices (fast/small vs slow/large tonnage)
Stock investment layer adds a distinct economic-game twist beyond typical pick-up-and-deliver
Strong production values and thematic presentation
criticised: Can feel dry and spreadsheet-like at times, heavy on optimization
Worker placement can create downtime, especially at higher player counts
Rules and market/stock interactions have a learning curve up front
Some swinginess from market price movements outside a player's control

interaction.kind: worker placement competition plus indirect market and stock-price interaction

scoring.why: Final standing comes mainly from accumulated cash plus the value of stock holdings in the various shipping companies
